result.title: Estimation of Propagated Risk in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
result.summary: Large Language Model (LLM) based multi-agent systems introduce a distinctive reliability challenge in which actions taken by upstream agents can affect the correctness of downstream agents. While prior work has investigated error propagation and developed methods for estimating uncertainty inherited from upstream agents, existing approaches do not explicitly model how realized sender-receiver interactions contribute to downstream error risk under different sender correctness states. In this work, we study agent-level error-risk estimation from multi-agent execution traces. We propose Interaction-Effect Propagation (IE-Prop), an interaction-conditioned model that learns separate effects for correct and incorrect upstream agents. For each sender-receiver interaction, the model combines these conditional effects using the sender's estimated error risk, and recursively propagates the resulting risk estimates through the execution graph. We evaluate our approach across three multi-agent architectures and three benchmarks. Across all evaluated architectures, our approach raises the final-node AUROC over the established baseline by approximately 0.05 points on average. Furthermore, tracking risk across multiple agent steps contributes a distinct +0.03 AUROC gain in sequential systems. These results show that realized inter-agent interactions provide predictive information beyond receiver-local evidence, while the value of multi-step risk tracking depends on the system's information-flow structure.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究 LLM 多智能体执行轨迹中的智能体级错误风险估计，提出 IE-Prop：为上游正确的与出错的两类情形分别学习交互效应，再按发送方的估计错误风险加权合并，并沿执行图递归传播风险；在三类多智能体架构与三个基准上验证，末节点 AUROC 平均提升约 0.05。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽非视觉工作，但其「按上游正确/错误状态条件化、沿计算图递归传播风险」的思路，可能可供核查于 LVR 中多步推理状态的可靠性估计、中间步骤贡献分配与是否继续计算的判断。
